title: First Strand cDNA Synthesis Protocol
author: Ben Kuipers
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8bmhsk6

steps.title: Prepare reaction mixture on ice
steps.instruction: In a sterile, nuclease‑free tube kept on ice, add the following in order: Template RNA (100 ng; range 1 pg–5 µg), Random Hexamer (1 µl, 100 pmol), dNTP Mix (1 µl, to give the final concentration specified by the kit), and nuclease‑free water up to a total volume of 14.5 µl.

substeps.instruction: Add Template RNA (100 ng; 1 pg–5 µg).
Add dNTP Mix (1 µl, final concentration).
Add nuclease‑free water to bring volume to 14.5 µl.

steps.title: Optional denaturation for GC‑rich RNA
steps.instruction: If the RNA is GC‑rich or highly structured, gently mix, briefly centrifuge, then incubate at 65 °C for 5 min, chill on ice, briefly centrifuge again, and keep the tube on ice.

substeps.instruction: Place the tube on ice to chill.
Keep the tube on ice until the next step.

steps.title: Mix and centrifuge briefly
steps.instruction: After assembling the reaction (and any optional denaturation), gently mix the contents and give a brief centrifugation to collect liquid at the bottom of the tube.

substeps.instruction: Gently vortex or flick the tube to mix.
Briefly centrifuge to collect the mixture.

steps.title: Thermal incubation of reverse transcription
steps.instruction: Place the tube in a thermocycler and run the following temperature program: 25 °C for 10 min, then 50 °C for 30 min (increase to 65 °C for GC‑rich RNA), followed by 85 °C for 5 min.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 50 °C for 30 min (or 65 °C for GC‑rich RNA).

steps.title: Finalize and store cDNA
steps.instruction: The first‑strand cDNA is now synthesized and can be used directly for downstream applications or stored as required.
